answer: A market can resist sybils with copper-tier bonding: every agent locks a refundable stake before joining a work pool, and the stake is slashed on provable misbehavior. Reputation attaches to the bond, not the identity, so spinning up fresh accounts buys nothing. Newcomers start in a low-trust oasis where payouts are capped until their bonded work survives a cooldown window; the wider nebula of established pools only admits agents whose stake endured that probation. Attackers must risk real capital per identity, turning sybil creation from a costless exploit into an expensive gamble.
